test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A can finish a work in 2 days and B can do the same work in 52 days. B worked alone for 26 days and left the job. In how many days can A alone finish the remaining work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work (LCM of 2, 52) = **52 units**.

Efficiency of **B** = 52 ÷ 52 = **1 unit/day**.

Work done by **B** in 26 days = 26 × 1 = **26 units**.

Remaining work = 52 − 26 = **26 units**.

Efficiency of **A** = 52 ÷ 2 = **26 units/day**.

Time for **A** to finish = 26 ÷ 26 = **1 day**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 day.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **A** = 2 days, Time taken by **B** = 52 days.

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 **A** 2 52 26 
 **B** 52 1 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done by **B** in 26 days = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Work done by **B** = 1 × 26 = **26 units**

⇒ Remaining Work = Total Work − Work Done

⇒ Remaining Work = 52 − 26 = **26 units**

⇒ Time taken by **A** alone = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of A

⇒ Time taken by **A** = 26 ÷ 26 = **1 day**

**∴ The correct answer is 1 day.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency Concept

**Efficiency** is inversely proportional to the **time** taken to complete the work (Efficiency = Work ÷ Time).

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed in the **ratio of work done** or the **ratio of efficiencies** if they work for the same duration.

Pipes and Cisterns

This follows the same logic where filling a tank is **positive work** and a leak (emptying) is **negative work**.</p
